faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Spinal Pedicle Screw suitable for Polyaxial pedicle screw for spinal fixation?
faq.a: Titanium Spinal Pedicle Screw uses Ti-6Al-4V ELI because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address spine fixation operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Spinal Pedicle Screw?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Spinal Pedicle Screw is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for polyaxial pedicle screw requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Spinal Pedicle Screw require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. polyaxial pedicle screw components require Electropolishing + passivation per ASTM F86 (20-30% HNO3, 30min @50C) achieving Ra <0.2um for implant-grade finish — tailored for polyaxial pedicle screw application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.
